paper_metadata.title: On the potential of quantum walks for modeling financial return distributions

summary: This paper studies discrete-time quantum walks as a model for financial return distributions, using time steps n = 20, 60, 100, 140, 180, and 220, with a Hadamard coin at θ = π/4 and decoherence probabilities p = 0.01, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 (or random-phase probability p~ = 0.01 to 1). The main quantitative findings are that the unitary walk has variance scaling quadratically in n, while the classical random walk scales as n^1/2, and decoherence drives the walk toward classical behavior while still producing fat tails for intermediate p values.

experiments.description: Discrete-time quantum walk model for financial return distributions, evaluated against classical return-distribution models using unitary and decohered quantum-walk dynamics.

algorithm.variant: Discrete-time quantum walk with SU(2) coin; Hadamard coin special case; decoherence via broken links or random phase coin
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Initial state specified explicitly; coin parameters chosen by sweep over representative values; decoherence simulations averaged over random realizations

problem_formulation.encoding_details: One-dimensional position basis |j⟩ represents return/price displacement; coin qubit controls left/right motion
problem_formulation.objective_function: Model the temporal evolution of asset prices and resulting return distributions P_j(n) via discrete-time quantum walk dynamics; compare distribution shape, skewness, variance, and entropy to classical models
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Decoherence introduced by stochastic broken links or random phase coin to interpolate toward classical diffusion

problem_instance.description: Synthetic financial-return modeling study; no real market dataset used. The paper studies generic return distributions and their qualitative properties.

dataset_specification.description: No empirical dataset; distributions generated from model dynamics and compared qualitatively to Gaussian, Lévy stable, and power-law forms

problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Parameter sweeps over coin angle, initial state, and decoherence probability; distributions averaged over 1000 simulations for decoherence cases; evaluation by visual comparison, skewness, variance, and Shannon entropy

noise_model.noise_type: decoherence via broken links or random phase coin; not hardware noise

implementation_details.classical_solver: Classical baselines: geometric Brownian motion, Lévy stable distributions, power-law distributions, classical random walk
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Histogram aggregation used to smooth quantum-walk distributions; normalization of distributions for comparison; computation of skewness, variance, and Shannon entropy

results.unit: nats, approximate maximum for uniform distribution shown

speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical random walk / classical diffusion models
speedup_claims.conditions: one-dimensional quantum walk circuit on a quantum computing device
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper cites prior work stating that a 1D quantum walk circuit can be implemented efficiently, but does not provide an explicit asymptotic speedup or benchmark.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Efficient implementation of a one-dimensional quantum walk circuit on a quantum computer is cited; no explicit asymptotic complexity derived in the paper
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Not explicitly characterized; classical random walk / distribution fitting baselines only

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: No resource counts, qubit counts, or asymptotic complexity are reported; the paper is a theoretical/simulation study of quantum-walk dynamics with parameter sweeps over n = 20, 60, 100, 140, 180, 220 and decoherence averaging over 1000 simulations.
limiting_factors: Classical baselines are only distributional references (GBM, Lévy stable, power law, classical random walk)
The paper focuses on modeling flexibility and qualitative distributional properties rather than computational advantage

notes: No specific hardware or framework is reported; the paper is a theoretical/simulation study of discrete-time quantum walks.
num_qubits is not explicitly stated because the paper formulates the walk in an abstract position⊗coin Hilbert space; a concrete qubit count is not given.

The paper states that a one-dimensional quantum walk circuit can be implemented efficiently on a quantum computing device, but does not provide a formal speedup claim or asymptotic complexity comparison.
The authors explicitly present the work as a theoretical comparison of quantum-walk-generated return distributions against classical models.
They do not demonstrate practical quantum advantage.
